## Summary

All 17 families retain distinct Pfam boundaries and assay-separated causal graphs; 3 actionable grounding/taxon findings remain open for Stage 5 grouped remediation.

## Scientific And Domain Assessments

### Cohort family boundaries and separated assay causal graphs

scope: supported. Targets: PF01680, PF01732, PF01865, PF01875, PF01914, PF01931, PF01934, PF01935, PF01936, PF01938, PF01939, PF01951, PF01956, PF01977, PF01980, PF01985, PF02410.

All 17 reviewed Pfam families represent distinct evolutionary domains and biochemical or cellular mechanisms (PLP synthesis, IgM cleavage, fimbrial phase switching, receptor-coupled migration, amidoxime reduction, NTP pyrophosphatase/Golgi export, antitoxin AMPylation, RNA/DNA helicase, mRNA decapping, cold-shock RNA binding, mismatch endonuclease, tRNA ligase activation, ER membrane insertion, FDC1 decarboxylation, tRNA t6A methylation, chloroplast CRM intron splicing, and ribosomal silencing). Stage 2 and Stage 3 partner/substrate UniProtKB groundings on the 14 updated overlays preserve exact tested organism and construct scope.

### Open causal-graph taxon and protein-node grounding gaps in PF02410, PF01980, and PF01985

representation: concern. Targets: PF01980, PF01985, PF02410.

Three overlays in the cohort have unambiguous single-species/single-protein mappings in family_mapping that are missing on specific causal graphs or nodes: PF02410 (ecoli-rsfs-deletion-media-shift missing taxon: NCBITaxon:83333), PF01980 (10 Kimura 2014 E. coli TrmO graphs missing taxon: NCBITaxon:83333 and 2 Thr3/Thr4 variant graphs missing UniProtKB:P28634 grounding on signal), and PF01985 (maize-mcrs1-magnesium-retention-2005 and maize-mcrs1-rna-deletions-2005 missing UniProtKB:Q9FYT6 grounding on mature CRS1-bound RNA retention STATE nodes).

## Findings

### pf02410-media-shift-graph-missing-taxon: Add explicit NCBITaxon:83333 taxon to ecoli-rsfs-deletion-media-shift causal graph

minor / open / confirmed; issue key: pf02410-media-shift-graph-missing-taxon.

In curation/families/PF02410.yaml, causal graph ecoli-rsfs-deletion-media-shift models whole-gene b0637 (rsfS, UniProtKB:P0AAT6, JW5090) deletion in Escherichia coli BW25113 derivatives (NCBITaxon:83333) from Hauser et al. 2012 (PMID:22829778), but omits taxon: NCBITaxon:83333 even though sibling graph ecoli-rsfs-preassociation in the same overlay explicitly specifies taxon: NCBITaxon:83333.

### pf01980-ecoli-trmo-graphs-missing-taxon-and-thr-variant-grounding: Add NCBITaxon:83333 to ten Kimura 2014 E. coli TrmO causal graphs and ground Thr3/Thr4 EcTrmO methylation readout nodes to UniProtKB:P28634

minor / open / confirmed; issue key: pf01980-ecoli-trmo-graphs-missing-taxon-and-thr-variant-grounding.

In curation/families/PF01980.yaml, ten Kimura et al. 2014 (PMID:24901881) Escherichia coli K-12 / BW25113 TrmO (UniProtKB:P28634) causal graphs (ectrmo-native-trna-deletion-2014, ectrmo-complementation-2014, ectrmo-thr3-binding-2014, ectrmo-thr3-methylation-2014, ectrmo-native-mixed-substrate-2014, ectrmo-residue-perturbations-2014, ectrmo-thr3-identity-loss-2014, ectrmo-thr4-identity-gain-2014, ectrmo-thrl-reporter-wt-background-2014, ectrmo-thrl-reporter-tcda-background-2014) omit taxon: NCBITaxon:83333 even though sibling E. coli K-12 graphs (tsaa1-thra-reporter-lb-1998, tsaa1-thra-reporter-mops-1998) in the same overlay specify taxon: NCBITaxon:83333. In addition, ectrmo-thr3-identity-loss-2014 and ectrmo-thr4-identity-gain-2014 omit grounding: [UniProtKB:P28634] on their EcTrmO-dependent methyl-incorporation readout nodes (signal), leaving those two graphs with zero grounded protein nodes despite explicit family_mapping to P28634.

### pf01985-mcrs1-retention-state-nodes-missing-q9fyt6-grounding: Ground mature CRS1-bound RNA retention state nodes in maize-mcrs1-magnesium-retention-2005 and maize-mcrs1-rna-deletions-2005 to UniProtKB:Q9FYT6

minor / open / confirmed; issue key: pf01985-mcrs1-retention-state-nodes-missing-q9fyt6-grounding.

In curation/families/PF01985.yaml, causal graphs maize-mcrs1-magnesium-retention-2005 (retained-rna: Fraction of atpF RNA retained with protein) and maize-mcrs1-rna-deletions-2005 (d1-retention, d4-retention, loop-retention: mature CRS1-bound RNA retention readouts) from Ostersetzer et al. 2005 (PMID:15598799) explicitly map to Zea mays mature CRS1 (UniProtKB:Q9FYT6, taxon: NCBITaxon:4577) in family_mapping, but omit grounding: [UniProtKB:Q9FYT6] on those protein-bound RNA retention STATE nodes, leaving both graphs with zero grounded protein nodes unlike sibling graph maize-mcrs1-intron-accessibility-2005 in the same source.

## Recommended Actions And Acceptance Checks

### remediate-stage4-cohort-grounding-and-taxon-findings

In Stage 5 (resolve_review_findings), add taxon: NCBITaxon:83333 to ecoli-rsfs-deletion-media-shift in PF02410.yaml and the ten Kimura 2014 E. coli TrmO graphs in PF01980.yaml, ground the Thr3/Thr4 EcTrmO methylation signal nodes in PF01980.yaml to UniProtKB:P28634, and ground the mature CRS1-bound RNA retention STATE nodes in PF01985.yaml to UniProtKB:Q9FYT6, recording canonical EDIT history events and regenerating projections.

- All three overlays record canonical EDIT history events and regenerate data/families/*.yaml cleanly.
- Every causal graph in PF02410, PF01980, and PF01985 has at least one grounded protein node and explicit taxon where single-species attribution is unambiguous.
- just qc and kg_microbe_workflows validate-evidence pass.

## Category Boundaries

- retain: PF01680, PF01732, PF01865, PF01875, PF01914, PF01931, PF01934, PF01935, PF01936, PF01938, PF01939, PF01951, PF01956, PF01977, PF01980, PF01985, PF02410. Each of the 17 Pfam entries is anchored to a distinct frozen InterPro/Pfam accession, structural fold, and experimental mechanism; none are redundant synonyms or chimeric family definitions warranting lumping or splitting. Within each family, biochemical, genetic, and reporter assays remain separated into distinct CausalGraph entries rather than lumped into unsupported multi-assay chains.

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR033755\ndescription: Members of this family are enzymes\

    \ those interpretations but uses distinct preparations and quench products.\n\
    \  evidence:\n  - reference: PMID:17189272\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source:\
    \ inspected_primary_full_text_and_figures\n    explanation: Figures support adduct\

    \ Some concentrations, mass descriptions and proposed structures remain inconsistent\
    \ or incompletely\n      documented.\n  - reference: PMID:18516049\n    supports:\
    \ PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: inspected_author_full_text_and_publisher_supplement\n\
    \    explanation: C2 ketone/C1-N observations and S5 nitrogen-labeling qualify\
    \ the early structural proposal.\n      Acid/urea-derived Z2 is explicitly not\
    \ a native enzymatic intermediate; the proposed complete chemical\n      pathway\
    \ is not fully directly observed.\n  notes: Preserve the 2008 follow-up in evidence/PF01680/hanes-2008-nmr-boundaries.txt.\
    \ Resolve full tagged\n    clone sequences, WT Pdx2 tag matching, 0.4 mM versus\
    \ 0.4 uM G3P, pH7.5 versus pH8.0, and text/table\n    mass differences. Inspect\
    \ the 2008 JACS substrate study before assigning intrinsic DHAP isomerization;\n\
    \    inspect the 2011 second-site and 2015 Geobacillus results before extending\
    \ the chemical sequence.\n    Assess plant/fungal and other microbial members\
    \ independently. No ammonia-channel geometry, physiological\n    phenotype or\
    \ family-wide mechanism is established by these graphs. Partial scientific self-review;\n\
    \    remain IN_PROGRESS.\n  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-11'\ncausal_graphs:\n\
    - graph_id: pdxs-partner-glutaminase-readout\n  title: PdxS addition increases\
    \ the partner glutaminase readout\n  scope: Purified untagged Bacillus subtilis\
    \ 168 YaaD/PdxS and YaaE/PdxT in Raschle 2005 supplement S2A.\n    This is the\
    \ same experiment retained from the partner perspective in PF01174, not an independent\
    \ replication.\n  context: 4 uM each protein when present, 300 ul, 50 mM Tris-Cl\
    \ pH 8.0, 10 mM glutamine, 0.5 mM APAD,\n    7 U bovine glutamate dehydrogenase,\
    \ 37 C; monitor A363. Individual-protein controls remain near background.\n  family_mapping:\
    \ P37527/PDXS_BACSU is strain-168 PdxS/YaaD, 294 aa, sequence version 3; exact\
    \ InterPro\n    sequence match and PF01680 7-212. Genomic cloning, sequencing\
    \ and N-terminal protein checks support\n    the association. The full untagged\
    \ protein, including residues outside this interval, was tested.\n  scope_status:\

    \    subject: add-pdxs-to-pdxt-glutamine\n    predicate: increases\n    object:\

    \   directness: DIRECT\n    support: OBSERVED\n    evidence_kind: EXPERIMENTAL\n\

    \      snippet: glutaminase activity\n      explanation: Supplement S2A and main\

    - graph_id: pdxs-joint-plp-product\n  title: The joint PdxS and PdxT reaction\

    \ 2 and supplemental S3; retain both the\n        reported product and its analytical\

    \ 4 preincubates R5P with each protein for 3 h at 37 C, compared with its no-R5P\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR022382\ndescription: This is the serine protease domain\
    \ of MIP (Mycoplasma immunoglobulin protease), a protein\n  that is related to\
    \ pathogenicity of animal and human pathogenic Mycoplasmas [[cite:PUB00098027],[cite:PUB00098028],[cite:PUB00098029],[cite:PUB00151017]].\n\
    \  This protein functions together with the Ig binding protein M (MIB) to evade\
    \ host Ig-mediated defense\n  against the MIB-MIP system, which is a novel mechanism\
    \ that protects mycoplasma against host immune\n  response [[cite:PUB00098028],[cite:PUB00151017]].\
    \ MIB tightly interacts to the antigen-binding fragment\n  (Fab) and recruits\
    \ the MIP protease that is activated and cleaves the IgG heavy chain, disrupting\
    \ the\n  antigen binding site. Therefore, the MIB-MIP system appears to be crucial\
    \ to mycoplasma immune evasion\n  [[cite:PUB00151017]].\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01732\n\

    - graph_id: gm12-mib-mip-locus-deletion\n  title: MIB-MIP locus deletion changes\
    \ cellular cleavage and immune-serum agglutination\n  scope: Nottelet 2021 Figure\
    \ 5B/C/E/F, GM12-derived Mmc WT versus deletion of all four MIB-MIP pairs;\n \
    \   the single retained MIB83-MIP82 pair is a separate positive comparator, not\
    \ a rescue.\n  context: Cleavage assays use about 1e9 washed late-exponential\
    \ cells in 15 ul SP5 without FBS, 100 ng/ul\n    purified serum IgG or 2% albumin-depleted\
    \ D12 goat serum, 30 min at 37 C, supernatant immunoblot.\n    Agglutination is\
    \ a different overnight static 37 C assay; Methods give 4% serum and caption 2%.\
    \ D0\n    serum does not produce the same cellular IgM cleavage/agglutination\
    \ response.\n  family_mapping: The deleted cluster includes MIP82/MMCAP2_0582,\
    \ ACU78687.1 with PF01732 290-776, but\n    also three other MIPs and four MIBs.\
    \ Whole-locus effects cannot be attributed exclusively to this\n    protein or\
    \ its domain. Main Figure 5B establishes the design; exact strain lineage and\
    \ nucleotide\n    breakpoints in inaccessible supplements remain unverified here.\n\
    \  scope_status: PHENOTYPIC\n  taxon: NCBITaxon:436113\n  limitations: INDIRECT\
    \ genotype effects. Single-pair retention is not reintroduction complementation.\n\
    \    Anti-HRP IgG is not detectably cleaved by cells despite purified-system activity.\
    \ OD310 measures settled\n    aggregates, not growth. Results panel cross-references\
    \ are offset; actual Figure 5C/E/F is used. Low-resolution\n    visual inspection\
    \ supports qualitative direction, not numeric effect sizes or a domain-specific\
    \ mechanism.\n  nodes:\n  - node_id: whole-locus-deletion\n    label: Delete all\

    - graph_id: marc-solvent-growth-2020\n  title: MarC deletion improves growth under\
    \ two solvent challenges\n  scope: Babel2020 MG1655-derived deletion background\
    \ compared with the study's initial MG1655; not all\n    evolved mutations or\
    \ a direct efflux assay.\n  context: Figures 4/5, 37 C, M9 glucose 5 g/L. Isoprenol\
    \ 50 mM and butanol 5 g/L are separate conditions;\n    relative fitness is growth\
    \ rate divided by the reference rate in that condition.\n  family_mapping: E.\
    \ coli K-12 MarC P0AEY1/b1529/JW1522 sequence version 1, 221 aa, PF01914 5-217.\
    \ This\n    is reference mapping, not independent sequencing of historical strains\
    \ or proof of isolated-domain\n    function. The CGSC6300-derived experimental\
    \ stock has restored gatC, functional glrR and REP321j variation;\n    it is not\
    \ assumed identical to the canonical reference.\n  scope_status: PHENOTYPIC\n\
    \  taxon: NCBITaxon:83333\n  limitations: Strain 953 is delta-marC750::kanR; 960\
    \ expresses the M35stop fragment and 1087 carries\n    empty vector in the deletion\
    \ background. Fragment expression adds no significant benefit and is not\n   \
    \ wild-type complementation. Three biological replicates/SD; no exact bar estimates.\
    \ Vanillin does not\n    show a strong benefit. Transport chemistry and domain/residue\
    \ sufficiency remain unresolved.\n  nodes:\n  - node_id: deletion-isoprenol\n\
    \    label: MarC deletion background under 50 mM isoprenol\n    node_type: PERTURBATION\n\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR008201\ndescription: This family includes the toxic component\
    \ HepT of a type II toxin-antitoxin (TA) system, which\n  has RNase activity.\
    \ These proteins contain a HEPN (higher eukaryotes and prokaryotes nucleotide-binding)\n\
    \  domain and are neutralised through tri-AMPylation by the cognate antitoxin\
    \ MntA, containing a MNT (minimal\n  nucleotidyltransferase) domain [[cite:PUB00097221],[cite:PUB00097219],[cite:PUB00097220]].\
    \ HepT-MnA\n  form an heterooctamer (at a 2:6 ratio), a rare organisation for\
    \ this kind of TA systems. HepT dimerises\n  and enables the formation of a deep\
    \ cleft at the HEPN-domain interface, containing the RX4-6H motif\n  (where X\
    \ is any amino acid and the residue immediately after the conserved R is typically\
    \ a polar amino\n  acid) as the active site that functions as an RNA-cleaving\
    \ RNase. This type II TA system regulates cell\n  motility and confers plasmid\
    \ stability [[cite:PUB00097219]]. Due to the prevalence of these HEPN/MNT\n  modules\
    \ in bacteria and archaea, it has been suggested that these TA systems may also\
    \ play a role in\n  the environmental adaptation to extreme habitats [[cite:PUB00097220]].\n\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR002789\ndescription: This entry represents the central\
    \ domain found in archaeal proteins such as DNA double-strand\n  break repair\
    \ helicase HerA ([ec:3.6.4.12]). HerA is a helicase which is able to utilise either\
    \ 3' or\n  5' single-stranded DNA extensions for loading and subsequent DNA duplex\
    \ unwinding [[cite:PUB00076694]].\n  It forms a complex with NurA nuclease, this\
    \ complex has the 5'-3' DNA end resection activity and is\n  essential for cell\
    \ viability in the crenarchaeon Sulfolobus islandicus [[cite:PUB00076695]]. This\
    \ domain\n  includes the the central RecA-like catalytic core and a flanking four-helix\
    \ bundle [[cite:PUB00078094]].\n  The function of this prokaryotic domain is unknown.\
    \ It contains several conserved aspartates and histidines\n  that could be metal\
    \ ligands.\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01935\ndiscussions:\n- discussion_id:\
    \ pf01935-motor-domain-and-assay-boundaries\n  prompt: Resolve assay and construct\
    \ differences before generalizing a HerA chemo-mechanical cycle.\n  kind: CURATION_TODO\n\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR021139\ndescription: These domains are found in the eukaryotic\
    \ proteins typified by the Nedd4-binding protein\n  1 and the bacterial YacP-like\
    \ proteins (Nedd4-BP1, YacP nucleases; NYN domains). The NYN domain shares\n \
    \ a common protein fold with two other previously characterized groups of nucleases,\
    \ namely the PIN (PilT\n  N-terminal) and FLAP/5' --> 3' exonuclease superfamilies.\
    \ These proteins share a common set of 4 acidic\n  conserved residues that are\
    \ predicted to constitute their active site. Based on the conservation of\n  the\
    \ acidic residues and structural elements Aravind and colleagues suggest that\
    \ PIN and NYN domains\n  are likely to bind only a single metal ion, unlike the\
    \ FLAP/5' --> 3' exonuclease superfamily, which\n  binds two metal ions. Based\
    \ on conserved gene neighborhoods Aravind and colleagues infer that the bacterial\n\
    \  members are likely to be components of the processome/degradsome that process\
    \ tRNAs or ribosomal RNAs.\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01936\ndiscussions:\n\
    - discussion_id: pf01936-member-mapping-and-native-targets\n  prompt: Resolve\
    \ native RNA targets and construct-specific effects without transferring historical\

    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR002809\ndescription: This entry represents a group of\
    \ eukaryotic and archaeal proteins. Eukaryotic members include\n  EMC3, a subunit\
    \ of the ER membrane protein complex (EMC) required for protein folding [[cite:PUB00061987]],\n\
    \  and TMCO1, a ER calcium load-activated calcium channel [[cite:PUB00081416]].\
    \ Archaeal members may function\n  as insertases of the archaeal plasma membrane\
    \ [[cite:PUB00086930]].\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01956\ndiscussions:\n\
    - discussion_id: pf01956-member-and-context-coverage\n  prompt: Extend primary\
    \ coverage to TMCO1, archaeal Ylp1 and remaining EMC3 systems without transferring\n\
    \    mechanisms between them.\n  kind: CURATION_TODO\n  status: OPEN\n  rationale:\
    \ The retained experiments concern assembled human EMC, selected human/yeast EMC3\
    \ perturbations\n    and selected human TMCO1/OPTI client-biogenesis contexts,\
    \ not every member of this former DUF106 family.\n  evidence:\n  - reference:\
    \ PMID:27212239\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: primary_publication\n\
    \    explanation: TMCO1 calcium-channel abstract inspected; full constructs, electrophysiology\
    \ and cellular\n      controls remain unreviewed.\n  - reference: PMID:26256539\n\
    \    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: database\n    explanation: Archaeal\
    \ Ylp1 structural study is an imported citation lead, not yet an inspected insertion\n\
    \      assay.\n  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-12'\n  notes: Current\
    \ TMCO1 Q9UM00 v2 is 239 aa; shorter Q9UM00-1 lacks canonical 1-51, but historical\
    \ clones\n    remain unverified. Selected 2020 and 2022 abundance/topogenesis\
    \ effects are now retained. Review the\n    inaccessible 2016 channel experiments,\
    \ archaeal Ylp1, later native-client/holo-insertase work and\n    original genetics.\
    \ See evidence/PF01956/identity-and-boundaries.txt and tmco1-isoforms-and-constructs.txt.\n\
    \    All earlier corpus follow-ups remain open.\n- discussion_id: pf01956-insertion-mechanism-and-constructs\n\
    \  prompt: Resolve exact historical constructs and directly test the proposed\
    \ insertion intermediates.\n  kind: CURATION_TODO\n  status: OPEN\n  rationale:\
    \ Reconstitution establishes whole-complex activity; cellular fluorescence, growth\
    \ and localization\n    do not identify each molecular step or isolated EMC3 sufficiency.\n\

    \ reporter effects; S9 is proximity evidence and\n      the loop/thinning mechanism\
    \ is a model.\n  - reference: PMID:32494008\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source:\
    \ primary_publication\n    explanation: Figures1/3 support yeast phenotypes; Hxt3\
    \ RNA decreases and gross complex assembly controls\n      do not exhaust alternatives.\n\
    \  - reference: PMID:29242231\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: primary_publication\n\
    \    explanation: Figure4 and supplementary Methods support mixed-orientation\
    \ EMC reconstitution; Figure4C\n      timing, vesicle preparation assignment and\
    \ trypsin protocol remain qualified.\n  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-12'\n\
    \  notes: Verify variant plasmid sequences/junctions, endogenous-versus-exogenous\
    \ stoichiometry and yeast\n    alleles; inspect raw gels and unreviewed supplements.\
    \ Pleiner supplement calls an amber codon UGA.\n    Do not silently repair the\
    \ source or turn crosslinking, membrane thinning or putative gating into\n   \

    \    explanation: Figure5 and supplement1 support endogenous EAAT1 abundance effects;\

    \ phenotype-to-phenotype chain\n    or family-wide insertase/channel equivalence\
    \ is inferred.\ncausal_graphs:\n- graph_id: human-emc-reconstituted-insertion-2018\n\
    \  title: Purified human EMC supports SQS reporter insertion into vesicles\n \

    \ isolated EMC3.\n  context: Guna2018 Figure4C/D; matched empty versus EMC proteoliposomes.\
    \ Separate native-RRL and isolated\n    PURE-derived CaM-SQS preparations; protected\
    \ C-terminal 3F4 fragment measured by autoradiography.\n    Defined-complex assay\
    \ uses 0.5 mM EGTA, 32 C for 20 min, then proteinase K and fragment IP; four experiments\n\
    \    per graph, mean +/- SD.\n  family_mapping: The complex contains human EMC3,\
    \ current reference Q9P0I2 v3, 261 aa, PF01956 5-191.\n    The tag is on EMC5.\
    \ Historical EMC3 sequence is not independently verified, and EMC3 is only one\
    \ required\n    complex component.\n  taxon: NCBITaxon:9606\n  scope_status: MECHANISTIC\n\

    \ timing is not explicitly separated from the general 15-min RRL protocol.\n \
    \   Protected product is not native SQS catalytic activity; VAMP2 is a poorly\
    \ inserted comparison substrate,\n    not proof of universal specificity.\n  nodes:\n\

    \  activity the carboxy-lase was shown to require Mn2+ [[cite:PUB00020511]]. This\
    \ entry represents the\n  central RIFT-related domain.\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01977\n\

    \ 2a assays with 10 uM C and 10 uM added D, 5 mM PHB or vanillate, 18 h in anoxic\
    \ chamber;\n    two independent HPLC replicates. D alone and no-protein cofactor\
    \ mix are controls.\n  family_mapping: ShC Q9S4M7 sequence 1 contains PF01977\
    \ 106-312; its 7AE4/5/7 body matches. Added ShD\n    Q4R102 is a separate PF26358\
    \ partner. No isolated central-domain construct was tested.\n  taxon: NCBITaxon:29345\n\
    \  scope_status: PHENOTYPIC\n  limitations: Addition establishes increased endpoint\
    \ conversion, not the exact allosteric route. C-alone\n    vanillate activity\
    \ is low but not uniformly zero; occupancy, assembly and maturation remain possible\n\
    \    contributions.\n  nodes:\n  - node_id: add_d\n    label: Add cognate ShD\

    - graph_id: shvdccd-partner-stoichiometry-2021\n  title: Greater ShVdcD availability\
    \ increases PHB decarboxylation activity\n  scope: ShC at fixed concentration,\
    \ reconstituted with substoichiometric or excess ShD.\n  context: Reconstitution\
    \ ShC 50 uM, ShD 10 or 200 uM, prFMN and Mn 200 uM each. Assays use 0.25 uM C\n\
    \    and 100 uM non-degassed PHB, A247 over 3 h; three technical replicates and\
    \ three independent trend\n    repeats.\n  family_mapping: ShC Q9S4M7 PF01977\
    \ 106-312 within a multidomain enzyme; titrated ShD Q4R102 is a PF26358\n    partner,\
    \ not a second PF01977 domain.\n  taxon: NCBITaxon:29345\n  scope_status: PHENOTYPIC\n\
    \  limitations: Activity does not resolve an exact catalytic assembly stoichiometry\
    \ or separate binding,\n    assembly and cofactor maturation/occupancy. Different\
    \ time points are reconstitution-dependent activities,\n    not direct single-molecule\
    \ transitions.\n  nodes:\n  - node_id: excess_d\n    label: Increase D:C from\
    \ 0.2 to 4 at fixed ShC\n    node_type: PERTURBATION\n    grounding:\n    - UniProtKB:Q9S4M7\n\
    \    - UniProtKB:Q4R102\n  - node_id: phb_rate\n    label: Measured PHB decarboxylation\
    \ rate\n    node_type: ACTIVITY\n  edges:\n  - edge_id: excess-d-increases-rate\n\
    \    subject: excess_d\n    predicate: increases\n    object: phb_rate\n    mechanism:\
    \ Excess D yields a higher activity plateau; at 90 min approximately 16.5-18.0\

    \ region, 16 Chimera morph models,\n    DFT Int2/Int3Quinoid and Vina docking.\

    \ cofactor sufficiency assay.\n  context: FDC protein precipitation with 1-to-1\

    \    without a separate rescue plot.\n  family_mapping: Donor and recipient FDC\
    \ are whole YDR539W preparations, reference-related to Q03034\n    with PF01977\

    \  family_mapping: Recipient whole FDC/YDR539W is Q03034-reference-related, PF01977\

    \ rescue series, exact dose\n    and established neutralization-matched controls.\

    \ endpoints,\n    not initial-rate comparisons. Fresh cells at OD600=1 are added\

    - graph_id: scfdc-anfdc-based-gate-hypothesis-2019\n  title: AnFdc-based docking\
    \ suggests a steric route for I330A substrate access\n  scope: Computational interpretation\
    \ of an AnFdc receptor using ScFdc residue numbering; not an observed\n    ScFdc\
    \ intermediate.\n  context: 'Sec6/20 and Figure 4c/d: rigid AutoDock Vina 1.1.2\
    \ with AnFdc 4ZA7, 20-A and 10-16-A grid\n    searches; substrate 1w. Reference\
    \ alignment maps ScQ192/ScI330 to AnQ190/AnI327.'\n  family_mapping: ScFdc/FDC1/YDR539W\
    \ is related to Q03034 sequence 1 (503 aa); PF01977 is 119-320, PF20695\n    14-102\
    \ and PF20696 328-464. The 2019 full plasmid insert is not independently verified;\
    \ see evidence/PF01977/scfdc-substrate-scope.txt\n    M/M1.\n  taxon: NCBITaxon:4932\n\
    \  scope_status: HYPOTHETICAL\n  limitations: Model coordinates and the exact\
    \ mutant receptor preparation were not retrieved or rerun.\n    Experimental I330A/V\
    \ effects are separate, confounded whole-cell comparisons. I330 lies outside PF01977.\n\
    \    The F133A energy label is inconsistent with I330A context; no F133A result\
    \ or corrected affinity is\n    invented. Geometry/planarity associations are\
    \ not a proven catalytic trajectory.\n  nodes:\n  - node_id: modeled_mutation\n\
    \    label: I330A substitution in the AnFdc-based model, using Sc numbering\n\
    \    node_type: PERTURBATION\n    grounding:\n    - UniProtKB:Q03034\n    - UniProtKB:A2QHE5\n\
    \  - node_id: pose\n    label: Modeled favorable orientation of 1w double bond\
    \ relative to prFMN\n    node_type: STATE\n  edges:\n  - edge_id: modeled-gate-relief\n\
    \    subject: modeled_mutation\n    predicate: enables\n    object: pose\n   \
    \ mechanism: The proposed Q192/I330 gate narrows substrate access; replacing the\

    curation_status: IN_PROGRESS\nsource_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/PF01980\n\
    counters:\n  proteins: 8639\n  matches: 8684\n  proteomes: 7015\n  taxa: 12908\n\
    \  structures: 6\n  alphafold_models: 5968\n  domain_architectures: 76\nprovenance:\n\

    \  sha256: 17fb625876c9326ed284263a47bcd84e0d7844a31c040dc06cd2260c36f1c383\n\
    \  generated_at: '2026-10-10T07:44:21.614711Z'\n  source_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/\n\
    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR023370\ndescription: This family includes members such\
    \ as TrmO (tRNA-methyltransferase O) also known as YaeB,\n  which contains a single-sheeted\
    \ beta-barrel structure. TrmO is an AdoMet-dependent methyltransferase\n  responsible\
    \ for m6t6A formation [[cite:PUB00086552]]. Its human homolog, is responsible\
    \ for formation\n  of m6t6A37 in cytoplasmic tRNASer. Lack of TrmO decreases attenuation\
    \ activity of the thr operon, indicating\n  that N6 methylation of m6t6A37 ensures\
    \ efficient decoding of ACY codons [[cite:PUB00137799]]. In bacteria\n  and eukaryotes,\
    \ TrmO has a C-terminal domain containing the conserved DPRxxY motif. Where the\
    \ Asp194\n  and Arg196 in this motif of E. coli TrmO are necessary for N6-methylation.\
    \ However, no archaeal YaeB\n  has a C-terminal domain containing the DPRxxY motif\
    \ that is conserved in bacterial and mammalian TrmO\n  homologs [[cite:PUB00086552]].\
    \ This entry represents the N-terminal domain of TrmO.\ncuration_history: history/records/PF01980\n\

    \  generated_at: '2026-10-10T07:44:21.614711Z'\n  source_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/\n\
    interpro_id: InterPro:IPR001890\ndescription: Escherichia coli YhbY is associated\
    \ with pre-50S ribosomal subunits, which implies a function\n  in ribosome assembly.\
    \ GFP fused to a single-domain CRM protein from maize localises to the nucleolus,\n\
    \  suggesting that an analogous activity may have been retained in plants [[cite:PUB00043747]].\
    \ A CRM domain\n  containing protein in plant chloroplasts has been shown to function\
    \ in group I and II intron splicing\n  [[cite:PUB00044700]]. In vitro experiments\
    \ with an isolated maize CRM domain have shown it to have RNA\n  binding activity.\
    \ These and other results suggest that the CRM domain evolved in the context of\
    \ ribosome\n  function prior to the divergence of Archaea and Bacteria, that this\
    \ function has been maintained in\n  extant prokaryotes, and that the domain was\
    \ recruited to serve as an RNA binding module during the evolution\n  of plant\
    \ genomes [[cite:PUB00043747]]. YhbY has a fold similar to that of the C-terminal\
    \ domain of translation\n  initiation factor 3 (IF3C), which binds to 16S rRNA\
    \ in the 30S ribosome [[cite:PUB00019352]][[cite:PUB00019353]].\ncuration_history:\
    \ history/records/PF01985\ndiscussions:\n- discussion_id: pf01985-bacterial-allele-and-preparation-controls\n\

    \ an rrmJ promoter region; the later preparation comparison\n    does not explicitly\

    \ addback restores co-IP rather\n      than ribosome maturation.\n  - reference:\
    \ PMID:17337586\n    supports: PARTIAL\n    evidence_source: primary_methods_table1_and_figures5_6\n\
    \    explanation: JM4690 has a cold-growth phenotype; Figure6 peak ratios are\
    \ relative readouts with unresolved\n      BW25113 culture-temperature matching.\n\
    \  posed_by: Codex\n  posed_date: '2026-10-16'\n  notes: evidence/PF01985/coverage-and-gaps.txt\
    \ retains exact allele, panel-strain, promoter-sparing rescue\n    and addback-dose\
    \ follow-ups. Do not conflate YhbY with YbeY or YhbO.\n- discussion_id: pf01985-crm-constructs-and-family-coverage\n\

    \ isolate atomic contacts; multivalent mature\n    CRS1 and isolated GST-CRM3\

    \  generated_at: '2026-10-10T07:44:21.614711Z'\n  source_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/entry/pfam/\n\
    description: This family is expressed by almost all bacterial and eukaryotic genomes\
    \ but not by archaea.\n  Its function is to down-regulate protein synthesis under\
    \ conditions of nutrient shortage, and it does\n  this by binding to protein L14\
    \ of the large ribosomal subunit, thus acting as a ribosomal silencing\n  factor\
    \ (RsfS) by blocking the joining of the ribosomal subunits [[cite:PUB00064845]].\
    \ This family is\n  structurally homologous to nucleotidyltransferases.\ncuration_history:\
    \ history/records/PF02410\ncausal_graphs:\n- graph_id: ecoli-rsfs-preassociation\n\
    \  title: E. coli RsfS suppresses ribosome association and oligo(Phe) synthesis\n\
    \  scope: Purified N-terminal His6-tagged E. coli b0637 RsfS, called RsfA in the\
    \ paper, expressed in BL21(DE3);\n    E. coli ribosomal subunits and purified\
    \ translation factors.\n  context: Preincubate 18 pmol 50S with 180 ug poly(U)\
    \ and with or without 360 pmol RsfS in 90 uL for\n    10 min at 37 C, then 10\
    \ pmol 30S for 10 min. Buffer contains 20 mM HEPES pH 7.6 at 0 C, 4.5 mM Mg\n\
    \    acetate, 150 mM K acetate, 4 mM beta-mercaptoethanol, 2 mM spermidine and\
    \ 0.05 mM spermine. Sister\n    aliquots undergo sucrose gradients or precharged\
    \ Phe-tRNA/factor-dependent synthesis for 2 min at\n    30 C.\n  family_mapping:\
    \ b0637 maps to UniProtKB:P0AAT6, sequence version 1, 105 residues; PF02410 spans\
    \ 9-104.\n    The experiment uses the tagged protein, not an isolated domain interval.\n\
    \  scope_status: MECHANISTIC\n  taxon: NCBITaxon:83333\n  limitations: The two\
    \ endpoints are measured separately in sister aliquots, not independent replication.\n\
    \    Preassembled programmed 70S does not show the same strong suppression; no\
    \ literally zero effect is\n    claimed. Steric contacts from docking and binding\
    \ assays are not separate observed causal steps. Human\n    mitochondrial and\
    \ later pre-50S biogenesis contexts remain separate.\n  nodes:\n  - node_id: rsfs-preincubation\n\
    \    label: RsfS addition before 30S-50S association\n    node_type: PERTURBATION\n\
    \    grounding:\n    - UniProtKB:P0AAT6\n  - node_id: associated-70s\n    label:\
    \ Associated 70S ribosome fraction\n    node_type: STATE\n  - node_id: oligo-phe-output\n\
    \    label: Poly(U)-dependent oligo(Phe) synthesis\n    node_type: PROCESS\n \
    \ edges:\n  - edge_id: rsfs-decreases-70s-association\n    subject: rsfs-preincubation\n\
    \    predicate: decreases\n    object: associated-70s\n    mechanism: Adding purified\
    \ RsfS before subunit association reduces the 70S fraction in the A260 sucrose-gradient\n\
    \      profile relative to the matched no-RsfS reaction.\n    directness: DIRECT\n\
    \    support: OBSERVED\n    evidence_kind: EXPERIMENTAL\n    evidence:\n    -\
    \ reference: PMID:22829778\n      source_url: https://journals.plos.org/plosgenetics/article?id=10.1371/journal.pgen.1002815\n\
    \      snippet: significantly reduces the fraction of 70S ribosomes\n      explanation:\
    \ Figure 4B, its caption and the poly(U)/gradient methods establish a purified-system\n\
    \        perturbation and measured assembly endpoint; Figure 4 was visually inspected.\n\
    \      cache_path: evidence/PF02410/hauser-2012-rsfs.txt\n      cache_sha256:\
    \ 227e2b3da32ac247a2cb804db6768c91b29af5b2e1fb8aad1ad31d91c38e6833\n    - reference:\
    \ https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/protein/uniprot/P0AAT6/entry/pfam/PF02410/\n\
    \      source_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/protein/uniprot/P0AAT6/entry/pfam/PF02410/\n\
    \      snippet: 'entry accession: PF02410'\n      explanation: Current member/domain\
    \ coordinates with paired UniProt locus and sequence-version facts;\n        identity\
    \ only, not independent causal evidence.\n      cache_path: evidence/PF02410/P0AAT6-identity.txt\n\
    \      cache_sha256: 9e6b9e5426c92b4ac5edc074c2bf03e2c63711e16b60cb34ee0d73e4f1849239\n\
    \  - edge_id: rsfs-decreases-oligo-phe\n    subject: rsfs-preincubation\n    predicate:\
    \ decreases\n    object: oligo-phe-output\n    mechanism: In the defined subunit-association\
    \ reaction, RsfS reduces incorporation of radiolabeled\n      phenylalanine into\
    \ oligo(Phe) to approximately one fifth of the no-RsfS control.\n    directness:\

    - graph_id: ecoli-rsfs-deletion-media-shift\n  title: RsfS deletion prolongs growth\
    \ adaptation after an LB-to-M9 shift\n  scope: Whole-gene b0637 deletion in E.\
    \ coli BW25113 derivatives versus matched wild type; separate cellular\n    phenotype\
    \ from the purified-subunit experiment.\n  context: Overnight LB cultures diluted\
    \ to OD600 0.005 in M9, 37 C and 200 rpm; OD600 monitored up to\n    40 h. Complementation\
    \ uses cassette-excised mutants and tac-driven C-terminal His-tagged RsfS induced\n\
    \    with 0.2 mM IPTG about 3 h after transfer.\n  family_mapping: The paper identifies\
    \ the deleted locus as b0637, corresponding to P0AAT6 and PF02410\n    at reference\
    \ residues 9-104. This is not a domain-specific perturbation or independent resequencing\n\
    \    of BW25113.\n  scope_status: PHENOTYPIC\n  limitations: The phenotype is\
    \ a prolonged growth plateau after initial growth, not immediate death or\n  \
    \  a measured energy deficit. Native-promoter complementation failed under the\
    \ tested conditions, while\n    induced tac expression rescued; the two are not\
    \ conflated. No direct metabolic chain from the in-vitro\n    assembly effect\
    \ is asserted.\n  nodes:\n  - node_id: rsfs-deletion\n    label: Whole-gene rsfS\
    \ deletion\n    node_type: PERTURBATION\n    grounding:\n    - UniProtKB:P0AAT6\n\
    \  - node_id: post-shift-delay\n    label: Prolonged post-shift growth plateau\
    \ and adaptation delay\n    node_type: PHENOTYPE\n  edges:\n  - edge_id: deletion-increases-adaptation-delay\n\
    \    subject: rsfs-deletion\n    predicate: increases\n    object: post-shift-delay\n\
    \    mechanism: The deletion strain shows an extended OD600 plateau after transfer\
    \ to M9; induced RsfS\n      complementation reduces the defect, supporting a\
    \ gene-dependent, condition-specific phenotype.\n    directness: INDIRECT\n  \
    \  support: OBSERVED\n    evidence_kind: EXPERIMENTAL\n    evidence:\n    - reference:\
    \ PMID:22829778\n      source_url: https://journals.plos.org/plosgenetics/article?id=10.1371/journal.pgen.1002815\n\
    \      snippet: The forced RsfA expression could heal the mutant phenotype\n \

    \ comparison and distinct\n        unsuccessful native-promoter and successful\
    \ tac complementation were inspected visually and in\n        text.\n      cache_path:\
    \ evidence/PF02410/hauser-2012-rsfs.txt\n      cache_sha256: 227e2b3da32ac247a2cb804db6768c91b29af5b2e1fb8aad1ad31d91c38e6833\n\

    \      source_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/api/protein/uniprot/P0AAT6/entry/pfam/PF02410/\n\
    \      snippet: 'orderedLocusNames: b0637, JW5090'\n      explanation: Locus-to-family\
    \ reference mapping, not proof of the cellular causal route.\n      cache_path:\
